overview: The click window packet is the only inventory interaction the server sees: window id, slot, button, action number and the dragged item. Anticheats use it to police click cadence and protocol correctness (Frequency InventoryA, NCP InventoryListener with FastClick and Gutenberg), and to catch movement while an inventory is open, the inventory-move cheat domain (CheaterDeleter InventoryMoveCheck, Negativity InventoryMoveProtocol). Because the packet is also the acknowledgement channel for server transactions, it feeds NCP's window-click and frequency bookkeeping.

checks.name: InventoryA (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Classic statistical inventory-click check: legit clicks arrive with variable spacing, clicker clicks do not.
checks.how_it_works: Samples the number of flying packets between WrappedPlayInWindowClick packets when fewer than 5 movements separate clicks and the player is not teleporting. At 5 samples it computes the standard deviation and outlier count; a deviation below 1 with zero outliers fails the check.
checks.detects: Inventory clickers and auto-totem/auto-armor modules that click slots at mechanically constant intervals.
checks.variations: InventoryB in the same package adds delay-pattern scoring; Degrade's InventoryA and azure's InvTweaks checks use the same low-variance template.

checks.name: InventoryMoveCheck (CheaterDeleter)
checks.purpose: Modern Fabric-side inventory-move check: position changes while a screen handler is open must agree with the player's velocity.
checks.how_it_works: A CDModule listening to movement, packet and damage callbacks. While the current screen handler is open and the player is not flying or in a collision cluster, position-change packets are validated: vertical rises with downward velocity flag immediately, and horizontal deltas that grow from a zero-velocity baseline flag after the 500 ms grace window. Closing the screen or taking damage resets the deltas.
checks.detects: Inventory-move cheats that walk or sprint while the inventory is open, including ghost-inventory movement spoofing.
checks.variations: CheaterDeleter's MovementModuleManager registers the check alongside SpeedCheck and PhaseCheck; Grim's CompensatedInventory and TickInventory simulate the same window state on the server.

checks.name: InventoryMoveProtocol (Negativity)
checks.purpose: Inventory-move scoring protocol: movement while an inventory is open is compared against the baseline captured at open time.
checks.how_it_works: Arms on InventoryClickEvent and InventoryOpenEvent, then on PlayerMoveEvent accumulates an alert amount: starting to sprint or sneak since the inventory opened adds points, and covering distance at or beyond walk speed since open adds more. When the inventory has been open for 3 ticks and the amount exceeds 2, it alerts with a confidence based on time open.
checks.detects: Inventory-move cheats that sprint, sneak or walk while an inventory is open, and velocity desync during inventory use.
checks.variations: Frequency's BadPacketsJ/M and Rammelkast's InventoryListener enforce the same no-movement-while-open rule on raw packets; Photon's InventoryMove module is the modern equivalent.

checks.name: InventoryListener suite (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: The canonical window-click check set: FastClick, InstantBow, Gutenberg, MoreInventory and Open, driven by inventory events and the click window packet.
checks.how_it_works: A CheckListener registering the inventory checks with per-player config and data, fed from Bukkit inventory events and the ProtocolLib InventoryAdapter wrapping PacketPlayInWindowClick. FastClick limits clicks per window per second, InstantBow flags bows fired without a charging period, Gutenberg caps creative item spam, MoreInventory catches rapid item nuking, and Open limits how often windows can be reopened.
checks.detects: Inventory clickers, instant-bow cheats, creative item spam, inventory nuking and window-open cycling.
checks.variations: AntiCheatPlus's InventoryListener and DynamicDev's InventoryListener expose the same fastclick idea on 1.7-1.8 servers; Frequency's InventoryA/B are the statistical descendants.
